risks: An unrequested referral may distress patients who are not ready to hear about palliative care, and extra referrals may lengthen waits for patients already referred; the trial adds no procedures.
consent: The trigger changes how referral is offered, and every patient can decline the appointment when the palliative care nurse calls. The research ethics board will be asked to approve an alteration of consent for the referral process and a waiver for routinely collected outcome data, with information posters in every clinic.
data: Outcome data are extracted within the hospital's secure environment; the analysis file carries study identifiers only; clinic results are shared with oncologists without naming individual clinicians.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients who live far from the centre, patients who need an interpreter, patients from communities where palliative care is associated with giving up, and patients with low health literacy may respond differently to an automatic referral. Calls use interpreters, telehealth appointments are offered, and uptake and outcomes are reported by distance, language and area deprivation.
effectiveness: The trial shows whether triggers change time at home and end-of-life care, not only when referral happens.
efficiency: Routine data and existing staff plus the added nurse time; the trigger build is a one-time informatics task.
costs: Added nurse time and the informatics build within the centre's budget; no payments to participants.
grants: A regional cancer research grant could fund the analysis and a later process evaluation; the trial can run without it.
partnerships: Medical oncology division, informatics, two patient partners with experience of advanced cancer, a family caregiver partner and the community hospice.
rebPath: Full research ethics board review of a stepped-wedge cluster trial with an alteration of consent for automatic referral and a waiver for routine outcome data, following ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki. The board has not yet reviewed the proposal, so the gate stays unknown and no trigger goes live before its decision.
limitations: Eight clusters limit power for small effects; oncologists may change behaviour before their clinic switches; routine data miss symptom burden and quality of life.
summary: Minimal added risk, an opt-out referral with the right to decline, consent alteration to be decided by the board, and equity reporting by distance, language and deprivation.
